actual_lwc_product.method: Read the archived product as NetCDF; for each field, count finite values > 0 and summarize positive values. These are mass concentrations, not mixing ratios.

actual_lsx_product.interpretation: LSX supplies surface state and diagnostics. LWC is the separate upper-air cloud/hydrometeor product.

source_line_map.evidence: Calls get_cloud_deriv with iflag_slwc=13 and separate slwc,cice arrays.
Flag 13 is New Smith-Feddes LWC; calls get_sfm_1d for slwc and cice separately and copies the two outputs independently.
Documents Smith-Feddes output and linear modeled liquid/ice dilution from -10 C to -30 C.
Thin cloud insertion creates separate cice/slwc according to the temperature thresholds.
Converts liquid/ice contents to kg/m3 and writes ICE, RAI, SNO, PIC as separate variables with separate comments.
Scales all hydrometeors by 2/dx; limits ice input concentration to autoconv_ice2sno before dividing by density; separately converts snow and precipitating ice.
Defines the current autoconversion bounds in kg/m3, including autoconv_ice2sno=0.0005.
Labels output ice as cloud ice mixing ratio, sno as precipitating snow, rai as precipitating rain, and pic as precipitating ice, units kg/kg.
Writes ice to QI, rain to QR, snow to QS, and precipitating ice/graupel to QG separately.
Uses LSX for surface temperature; reads the five LWC hydrometeors independently, checks kg/m3 units, maps ice to cloud_ice, divides contents by dry-air density, and reverses source vertical order.

independent_cap_audit.source_policy_note: This source envelope is a moment-feasibility diagnostic and is not evidence that source QICE should be moved to another mass reservoir.

retained_high_ice_evidence.interpretation: Same-13 retained evidence says all five input hydromass fields remain exactly equal through native initialization; QICE is full-domain state while observation support is limited. This supports inheritance as a possibility. Exact overlap of high/infeasible cells and support columns was not calculated in this trace.
